title: Newton's third law of motion (নিউটনের তৃতীয় গতি সূত্র)
placement: Book pages 84–86, topic 3.8: নিউটনের তৃতীয় গতি সূত্র (Newton's Third Law of Motion). Next to the boxed law, the action–reaction paragraph and চিত্র ৩.১২ (an apple and the Earth pulling each other).
description: Newton's third law (নিউটনের তৃতীয় সূত্র, pages 84–86, 3.8) as an experiment the student runs: two skaters face each other on a smooth floor, hands together; one tap and they push each other with the same steady 10 N for a moment. A pair of equal, opposite arrows is drawn, each on the body it acts on and named ("A-এর ওপর বল", "B-এর ওপর বল"), so the two never cancel; both skaters move off, and with unequal masses (50 kg and 100 kg) the lighter one accelerates twice as much (a = F/m, 0.2 and 0.1 ms⁻²). The third picture is the book's চিত্র ৩.১২: a 1 kg apple let go above the Earth, the pull on the apple and the pull on the Earth both 9.8 N, while the Earth's acceleration a = (m/M)g is 1.64 × 10⁻²⁴ ms⁻² (M = 5.98 × 10²⁴ kg), too small to draw. The panel is one action, one result, one rule: a big numbered button ("১ ধাক্কা দাও") whose same numbered badge rings the hands (a tap on a skater or the apple does the same), one result line and one rule that grows from a question to the book's boxed law, word for word. Honest notes on the view: smooth floor; for the apple, time 2 times slower and not to scale. Test tab: 5 questions (which force is the reaction, why the pair does not cancel, who accelerates more, the pair is equal for any masses, why the Earth does not visibly move). Phone-first, Bangla.
